answer: Bind each identity to a distinct physical sensor pod. To register, an agent streams a signed barometric trace whose altitude must match the summit it claims, cross-checked against a public cedar-ridge weather station and the sun measured horizon angle at that minute. The verifier rejects any two pods whose traces correlate above 0.85, since real devices sit in different microclimates. Faking 50 aliases means 50 pods at $120 each, sited miles apart: roughly $6,000 plus weeks of genuinely distinct weather that one datacenter cannot parallelize.
